comparator.name: Archaeology (Archeologie)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–27 OER for VU bachelor Archaeology, checked 2026-09-25
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 OER confirms the exact normalized Dutch-language Archeologie trajectory alongside a separate English-language Archaeology trajectory. Its ordinary 180-EC curriculum is 60 EC of ten compulsory first-year courses; 78 EC of thirteen compulsory post-propaedeutic courses; a 12-EC bachelor thesis in the Dutch trajectory; and 30 EC genuinely free third-year academic profiling space. Field School 1 and 2, materials research, digital archaeology and excavation-to-publication work are prescribed in the ordinary curriculum. The English-track thesis is the same role in a different language and not an extra component. Optional Field School 3 and optional Forensic Archaeology listed among practical teaching activities are not silently counted as compulsory. The OER curriculum table rather than illustrative admissions text establishes the credit accounting.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized source registration is B Archeologie with teaching language Dutch. The adopted 2026–27 OER formally distinguishes the Dutch-language Archeologie trajectory from English-language Archaeology; the Dutch trajectory and its 12-EC Bachelorscriptie Archeologie are selected.

exception.reason: The external major devotes 138 specified EC to archaeological and ancient-world education before its separate 12-EC archaeology thesis, leaving 30 EC of free choice. Required study spans prehistoric, Roman, medieval and early-modern European material cultures, archaeological source and object analysis, scientific and digital archaeology, two credited field schools, excavation-to-publication training and disciplinary theory. UCR has a small, valuable archaeology and heritage group, including Introduction to World Archaeology, Greek Archaeology and Heritage & Ancient Democracy, but it has no excavation training sequence, archaeometric/materials laboratory sequence, European prehistoric-to-medieval archaeology sequence or archaeological thesis requirement. Filling 24 UCR courses with mostly modern history, art, cultural theory or generic research methods would present neighbouring subjects as an Archaeology bachelor. No defensible closest 24-course UCR programme can be formed.
exception.curriculumContext: Article 11.1 of the adopted 2026–27 OER defines 60 EC propaedeutic, 78 EC compulsory post-propaedeutic units, 30 EC free academic choice and 12 EC bachelor thesis. Article 11.3 lists ten 6-EC first-year compulsory components; Article 11.4 lists thirteen 6-EC later compulsory components and the Dutch or English alternative 12-EC thesis. The target is the Dutch route. The explicit open choice is preserved instead of being populated with invented archaeology electives.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed the current 151-row enriched UCR workbook, including course profiles, descriptions, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability. MCCHEAM112 introduces world archaeology through material culture; MCCHEAM213 studies Greek archaeology; MCCHEAM315 connects Greek ancient democracy with material and heritage questions. MCCHEAM211 treats African art and heritage, MCCHEAM212 Mediterranean Renaissance art, and MCCHEAM111/312/316 art history and museums; these may contribute to an ancient cultures or heritage theme but do not replace systematic archaeological method. GOSHIST111/112/211/311/312 largely focus on modern, imperial or local historical subjects; GOSHIST213 includes ancient warfare but is not excavation archaeology. MCCMEDI112 uses “archaeology” metaphorically for media technology. General qualitative and quantitative methods and environmental field courses do not supply archaeological stratigraphy, supervised digs, finds processing, materials science or the VU research sequence. Thus a 24-course archaeology-led UCR alternative would require more than a handful of genuinely relevant archaeology courses and cannot pass the specific course-to-concept gate.
